canDo: Can take the initiative in a 3–4-minute interaction: explain, answer objections and find a solution.
review: Review the conditionnel, negation and questions.
output: Record each round; in the second round, the other person changes attitude.
checkpoint: Must include an active opening, at least 1 answer to an objection and an alternative solution.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a “negotiating / problem-solving” dialogue on TV5MONDE Apprendre B1 or RFI and pick out 3 polite requests (e.g. Est-ce que vous pourriez… / Si c'était possible, j'aimerais…); then do a 3-minute role-play with a friend or your phone: returning an item bought online, using at least 1 si + imparfait → conditionnel and 1 double object pronoun (je vous le renvoie, vous me les remboursez).

questions.why: Examples: cutting down trees vs leaves blocking gutters and winter light.
The ending quotes her own words.

V38-01.exZh: I’m well aware that the budget is limited, but the situation has changed.

V38-02.exZh: — It’s going well, isn’t it? — That’s exactly what worries me: I’m passing on my mistakes too.

V38-03.zh: Let me stop you there. (polite correction)
V38-03.exZh: Let me stop you there, politely: the page said “300 m from the beach”.

V38-04.exZh: People often give way hoping for a gesture in return, which almost never comes.

V38-05.exZh: Naming a real limit makes the rest of the negotiation credible.

V38-06.zh: On this point, I can’t go any further.
V38-06.exZh: I’ll lower the price by 10%, but on this point I can’t go any further.

V38-07.exZh: The more you defend your position, the harder it is to move without losing face.

V38-08.exZh: Work out in advance what you are ready to give up.

V38-09.exZh: About 60% of mediations end in a written agreement.

V38-10.zh: to see … through to the end
V38-10.exZh: Everyone must be able to finish what they are saying.

V38-11.exZh: A mediator doesn’t settle the dispute: they organise the dialogue.

V38-12.exZh: The agenda no longer covered the location.

V38-13.exZh: A young man pointed out that the noise after nine at night had nothing to do with them.

V38-14.exZh: It’s kind of you to invite me, but I can’t come on Saturday.

V38-15.exZh: I’d be glad if we could meet another time.

V38-16.exZh: I wanted us to talk about the bills again: the way they’re split seems unfair to me.

V38-17.exZh: — I’d like us to change how we split things. — Go ahead, I’m listening.

V38-18.zh: Thank you for listening to me.
V38-18.exZh: It’ll be done tonight. Thank you for hearing me out twice.

V38-19.exZh: I don’t want a voucher: I’m asking for a partial refund.

V38-20.exZh: Who can decide, and how soon?

V38-21.exZh: The sales assistant offers me a 150-euro voucher.

V38-22.exZh: Energy and water are adjusted in proportion to the nights spent there.

V38-23.exZh: Agreed in principle, but the rent stays the same.

V38-24.exZh: Keep the rent split in thirds? That seems reasonable to me.

V38-25.zh: to drop it, to let it go
V38-25.exZh: If the difference is ten euros, let’s drop it.

V38-26.zh: to ask for a second opinion
V38-26.exZh: I’d like a second opinion before deciding.

V38-27.exZh: You are fully entitled to see another doctor.

V38-28.zh: I wouldn’t have thought of that.
V38-28.exZh: Go to another hospital? I wouldn’t have thought of that.

V38-29.exZh: How can you ask for a second opinion without offending your doctor?

V38-30.exZh: Sorry to bother you, I have a problem with my order.

V38-31.zh: Would there be any way to …?
V38-31.exZh: Would there be any way to deliver the right model this week?

V38-32.zh: to make an effort, to meet someone halfway
V38-32.exZh: If you make an effort on the delivery time, I’ll agree to wait.

V38-33.exZh: I suggest we split the difference: you pay half the costs.

V38-34.exZh: Delivery on Tuesday morning? That works for me.

V38-35.zh: to ask to speak to the manager
V38-35.exZh: Since you can’t decide, I’m asking to speak to the manager.

V38-36.exZh: A polite refusal has three parts: acknowledgement, the refusal itself and an opening.

V38-37.zh: What would make you say yes?
V38-37.exZh: You’re turning down my proposal; what would make you say yes?

V38-38.exZh: I contacted after-sales service about the repair.

V38-39.exZh: You can exchange an item within thirty days.

V38-40.exZh: I took a screenshot of the page when I booked.

V38-41.exZh: Keep the receipt if you want to exchange the product.

V38-42.exZh: An overlong explanation arouses suspicion: the more you justify, the less you’re believed.

V38-43.exZh: If the first solution doesn’t suit, suggest an alternative.

V38-44.exZh: We finally found a compromise acceptable to everyone.

V38-45.exZh: A concession given for nothing is taken for granted.
